question.text: Under Section 212 of the Companies Act, 2013, which of the following can trigger an SFIO investigation?

answer.text: Receipt of a Registrar/Inspector report, a special resolution by the company, and a request from any Central or State Government department
Only receipt of a report from the Registrar or Inspector
Only a special resolution passed by the company requesting investigation
Only a request from any Department of Central or State Government

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Section 212(1) of the Companies Act, 2013, the Central Government may assign an investigation to SFIO upon receipt of a Registrar/Inspector report under Section 208, on a special resolution by the company seeking investigation, in the public interest, or on a request from any Central or State Government department. The Trap: Each of the listed triggers is independently valid under Section 212(1); none is exclusive. Picking any single trigger ignores the other equally valid triggers that the section enumerates. Note: Each Section 212(1) trigger stands on its own — an SFIO referral can come from a Registrar/Inspector report, a company's own special resolution, or a Government department's request, with no order of priority.
